decisive_items: Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105)
diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk
thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa
response.rationale: Hypopituitarism with diffuse pituitary/stalk swelling, elevated IgG4, and sphenoid sinus mucosal thickening strongly favor IgG4-related hypophysitis over lymphocytic hypophysitis or lymphoma.

rejected.why: Lymphocytic hypophysitis can cause hypopituitarism and pituitary swelling, but it does not explain the markedly elevated IgG4, elevated IgG4/IgG ratio, or systemic IgG4 suspicion.
Sellar lymphoma is unlikely given the diffuse inflammatory pituitary/stalk pattern, elevated IgG4, and absence of lymphoma-defining imaging or systemic features.
